title: Completing a Table of Function Compositions (Set II)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Complete the missing entries in the composition table for g(x), f(x), and (f o g)(x): (a) g(x) = 1/(x - 1), f(x) = |x|, (f o g)(x) = ?; (b) g(x) = ?, f(x) = (x - 1)/x, (f o g)(x) = x/(x + 1); (c) g(x) = ?, f(x) = sqrt(x), (f o g)(x) = |x|; (d) g(x) = sqrt(x), f(x) = ?, (f o g)(x) = |x|.
finalAnswer: \text{(a) } \frac{1}{|x - 1|},\quad \text{(b) } g(x) = x + 1,\quad \text{(c) } g(x) = x^2,\quad \text{(d) } f(x) = x^2

steps.title: Determine (f o g)(x) in Part (a) and g(x) in Part (b)
steps.explanation: In (a), substitute 1/(x - 1) into |x|. In (b), rewrite f(u) = (u - 1)/u = 1 - 1/u and set it equal to x/(x + 1) = 1 - 1/(x + 1) to obtain g(x) = x + 1.
steps.why: Rewriting (u - 1)/u as 1 - 1/u isolates u cleanly so we can solve f(g(x)) = x/(x + 1) for g(x).

steps.title: Use the Principal Square Root Identity in Part (c)
steps.explanation: Because the principal square root of x^2 is |x| for all real x, choosing g(x) = x^2 makes sqrt(g(x)) = sqrt(x^2) = |x|.
steps.why: For every real number x, sqrt(x^2) = |x| by definition of the non-negative principal root.

steps.title: Determine f(x) on the Domain of g in Part (d)
steps.explanation: In part (d), g(x) = sqrt(x) is defined only for x >= 0, where |x| = x = (sqrt(x))^2. Thus setting f(x) = x^2 gives f(sqrt(x)) = (sqrt(x))^2 = x = |x| on [0, infinity).
steps.why: On the domain x >= 0 of g(x) = sqrt(x), |x| coincides with x = (sqrt(x))^2.
